newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast late prods bow under NYMEX sell-off.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast late prods bow under NYMEX sell-off.

text.p: Late prices for U.S. West Coast refined product prices bowed under the weight of steep NYMEX declines, with trade thin as traders were scarred off by lower prices.
"Everyone was in shock about what happened on NYMEX," one broker said.
November heating oil expired down 2.12 cents to 66.34 cents a gallon, while November gasoline went off the boards a sharp 3.44 cents lower at 66.56 cents.
The steep decline came after December crude broke through key support levels and triggered computerised sell orders.

Spot prices for CARB-grade conventional regular gasoline eased 1.25 cents. Traders talked prices between 63.50 and 64.50 cents a gallon. Premium CARB in L.A. hovered about four cents over regular CARB.
Spot prices for Los Angeles conventional unleaded gasoline fell a cent in late trading to 60/61 cents a gallon. Premium gasoline stood five cents higher.
San Francisco conventional gasoline stayed one cent under L.A., at 59/60 cents. L.A. offers for low sulphur diesel were down a cent to 68/69 cents a gallon early.
